scope: Independent read-only current AnyHTTPClient/native Echo contract review; no new requests, probes, compilation or production setting change.

inference.kind: static control-flow inference, not captured request trace
inference.phase: preflight before the second guarded object creation
basis: The first folder ID was appended only after requestJSON returned successfully; the custom child call is next.
The second create uses an empty authorize closure.
raw catches every non-GET transport error and replaces it with writeUncertain.
The post-response account check converts its failure to known-ID recovery or writeUncertain for POST.
An unchanged Foundation.URLError therefore propagates from the initial checkAccount raw GET before POST dispatch.

findings: URLRequest.timeoutInterval is30 seconds. URLSession is ephemeral, cookies/cache disabled; the code changes no keepalive, pipelining, connection-count or framing setting.
The redirect delegate is stateless and only declines redirects. No application lock, semaphore or blocked main-actor delegate is held around data(for:).

Managed GET /auth returns gated account identity plus static capabilities immediately; it skips standalone account/wallet enumeration. Gate enter/leave lock only a generation admission counter and do not wait for SDK writes.
Echo server.Run/buildEcho configure no ordinary read/write/idle deadline. The one-second response write deadline belongs only to engine teardown cancellation.
Echo serializes JSON through encoding/json.Encoder and delegates Write to the underlying Go ResponseWriter; no hand-written content length or chunk framing was found.
Retained Python controls on the same native fixture successfully read fixed-length and chunked responses over one persistent HTTP/1.1 connection. This does not prove FoundationNetworking behavior.

separateRoutingObservation.sourceFact: The pprof route is mounted on root Echo outside the mobile-managed token gateway.

unsupportedConclusions: No justified blanket keepalive-off or longer deadline fix
No hierarchy20 PASS or Windows transport reliability claim
